_meta.description: ClickHouse round-trip fixtures for intDiv vs '/' divergence. CF-C4-RATIO-DIVOP-1.
_meta.constraint: NO live data. Fixtures are synthetic and exactly computed. CF-C2-NO-LIVE-1.
_meta.purpose: These fixtures prove that ClickHouse '/' on Int64 returns Float64 (not FLOOR), and that intDiv produces correct integer results. The kill-test: reverting one MV division from intDiv(...) to '/' causes the zero-denominator or divergent fixture to go RED.
_meta.gate: CF-C4-RATIO-DIVOP-1 — MUST bind before any MV DDL is authored.

intdiv_non_zero_remainder.description: 1/3 ratio → 3333 bp. intDiv(1 * 10000, 3) = intDiv(10000, 3) = 3333 (FLOOR). Float64: 10000/3 = 3333.333... which truncates to 3333 for positive (coincides with FLOOR for positives). Proof: intDiv and '/' agree for this case — the divergence is on ZERO-DENOM and larger inputs.
intdiv_non_zero_remainder.note: Non-zero-remainder: intDiv = 3333, float64 truncation = 3333 (positive coincidence). The bug is visible ONLY on zero-denominator days.

intdiv_non_zero_remainder.description: 7/3 ratio → 23333 bp. intDiv(7 * 10000, 3) = intDiv(70000, 3) = 23333 (FLOOR of 23333.33). float64: 70000.0/3 = 23333.333... truncates to 23333 in Int64 cast. Still agrees for positive non-edge cases.
intdiv_non_zero_remainder.note: Positive non-zero-remainder: intDiv == float truncation. Safe for positive values.

intdiv_zero_denominator.description: CRITICAL: zero denominator. rto_orders=1, total_shipments=0. intDiv with null-guard: if(total_shipments > 0, intDiv(rto_orders * 10000, total_shipments), NULL) → NULL. ClickHouse '/' without guard: 10000 / 0 → inf (Float64 +Inf). This is a real bug that PASSES all positive-integer tests.
intdiv_zero_denominator.kill_test: Removing the null-guard (using '/' instead of 'if(denom>0, intDiv(...), NULL)') causes this fixture to return INT64_MAX instead of NULL — the test must go RED.
intdiv_zero_denominator.note: CF-C4-RATIO-DIVOP-1: this is the canonical zero-denominator kill-test. Child-5 anomaly detection ingests INT64_MAX as a legitimate spike if not guarded.

intdiv_zero_denominator.description: zero denominator on AOV: net_sales=50000 paise, orders=0. intDiv with guard: NULL. Float64: 50000.0/0 = inf → INT64_MAX coercion.
intdiv_zero_denominator.kill_test: Without null-guard, aov_mu returns INT64_MAX on zero-order days.

float64_vs_floor_divergent.description: Float64-vs-FLOOR divergent case. This case is designed to expose a scenario where ClickHouse Float64 intermediate value, when cast to Int64, differs from intDiv result due to floating-point representation. Example: intDiv(2147483647 * 10000, 3) = intDiv(21474836470000, 3) = 7158278823333. Float64: 21474836470000.0 / 3 = 7158278823333.333... In Float64 (IEEE-754 double), 21474836470000 cannot be represented exactly (53-bit mantissa limit for large integers). The Float64 result may be 7158278823333.0 or 7158278823334.0 depending on rounding — this is where Float64 diverges from intDiv.
float64_vs_floor_divergent.float64_precision_note: For large integers (>2^53 = 9007199254740992), IEEE-754 double cannot represent all integers exactly. 21474836470000 > 2^44 but < 2^53, so it IS representable. However, the quotient 7158278823333.333 is NOT exactly representable; Float64 stores the nearest representable double.
float64_vs_floor_divergent.note: This case happens to agree for this specific value. The REAL divergence risk is at values > 2^53 where the integer itself is not exactly representable in Float64. The zero-denominator case (ch-rt-zero-1) is the concrete kill-test.

float64_vs_floor_divergent.description: Prorated misc expense: monthly_amount_mu=1000000 paise, days_in_month=28 (Feb 2026). intDiv(1000000, 28) = 35714 (FLOOR of 35714.285...). ClickHouse '/': 1000000.0/28 = 35714.285714...; toInt64 in ClickHouse truncates toward zero for positive → 35714. This case agrees. The ROUNDING_MODE_MISMATCH comes from Postgres ROUND_HALF_UP on the STORED legacy value, not from ClickHouse Float64 here.
float64_vs_floor_divergent.cf_constraint: CF-C4-PRORATED-DIVOP-1: use intDiv(monthly_amount_mu, toDaysInMonth(date)) — NEVER '30' constant
float64_vs_floor_divergent.note: Feb 2026 = 28 days. Feb 2024 (leap) = 29 days. A hardcoded '30' gives intDiv(1000000,30)=33333 — WRONG by 2381 paise (₹23.81/day). This is a bug, not a rounding delta.

float64_vs_floor_divergent.description: Hardcoded-30 constant bug exposure. monthly_amount_mu=1000000 paise, Feb 2026 (28 days). Wrong: intDiv(1000000, 30) = 33333. Correct: intDiv(1000000, 28) = 35714. Delta = 35714 - 33333 = 2381 paise (₹23.81/day). This is CF-C4-PRORATED-DIVOP-1 / CF-C4-DDR-MISC-PRORATE-1.
float64_vs_floor_divergent.cf_constraint: CF-C4-PRORATED-DIVOP-1: adjudication must NOT let this bug hide as ROUNDING_MODE_MISMATCH
float64_vs_floor_divergent.kill_test: A test that uses days=30 for February MUST go RED when compared against expected_correct_result=35714.

cogs_settings_change_delta.description: COGS_SETTINGS_CHANGE_DELTA: coq-settings-change mid-day. Full-recompute model produces zero delta vs legacy. Incremental MV model produces non-zero delta.
cogs_settings_change_delta.full_recompute_formula: 18 orders × 7500 paise (new coq, applied to ALL orders at recompute time) = 135000 paise
cogs_settings_change_delta.incremental_mv_formula: 10 orders × 5000 (old coq, captured before change) + 8 orders × 7500 (new coq) = 50000 + 60000 = 110000 paise
cogs_settings_change_delta.note: CF-C4-COGS-MV-REFRESH-1: full-recompute = zero delta vs legacy. Incremental MV = ₹250 error. Brain uses full daily recompute to match legacy exactly.
cogs_settings_change_delta.kill_test: If the model reverts to incremental MV, expected_brain_result would be 110000 ≠ 135000 — the test must go RED.
